Roads

How the Salt Road Got Its Name
The Salt Road crosses the moor in a long curve that no modern engineer would have drawn. Pack animals followed it from the coastal pans to the market towns inland.
1
Each mule carried about two hundred pounds of salt in woven panniers.
2
Related reading:
Mules and merchants on the moor
The road is mentioned in a charter of the twelfth century, but the name appears much later. A parish clerk wrote it down in a tax roll, probably because it was how local people already spoke of the track.
3
Today the path is a popular walk. Stone markers set every mile show how far travellers had to go before the next inn.
Notes
The earliest drawn route is on a parish map kept at the county archive.
The figure comes from a toll ledger of the fourteenth century.
The tax roll was rediscovered during repairs to the vestry roof.
